sources.title: Independent vector/Jacobian arithmetic and unit convention
sources.details: x=(1,2), f=2x=(2,4), y=(3,6); J_y=I+2I=3I; gradient of sum outputs=J_y^T(1,1)=(3,3). Single-feature h=.001 gives output delta3h=.003. f=0x gives identity y=x and sum-gradient(1,1). General output-row/input-column J_y=I+J_f; scalar sum gradient is column sums. No sample mean or denominator used; see permanent inspection-and-derivation.md.

claims.statement: 殘差連線把已有表示沿直接路與修正分支逐格相加，標準同形狀 identity residual 為 y=x+f(x)。
claims.scope: Identity shortcut of matching feature shape, without a post-addition operation; this standard architecture convention is not a claim that every broadcastable PyTorch addition is prohibited.

evidence.locator: Sec3.1/3.2, Eq1, Fig2, PDFp3 equality-of-dimensions paragraph and Eq2
evidence.supports: Defines residual F(x)=H(x)-x, y=F(x)+x via shortcut and elementwise addition; explicitly requires equal x/F dimensions for identity case and gives projection for changing dimensions.
Separates shortcut h, branch F and post-addition f; when shortcut and post-addition are identity, obtains exactly x_next=x+F(x), matching this toy's clean sum.

claims.statement: 直接路讓已有表示與反向敏感度有 identity 貢獻；分支可以學修正。這不保證訓練成功、總梯度必非零或原文完整可還原。

claims.scope: Direct additive contribution in clean identity residuals, not global invertibility or empirical language/training capability. A small branch value alone does not imply a small branch derivative; the statement refers to the direct route.

f=-x produced y=0 and total gradient0; tiny-valued sine branch at0 gave total gradient2, illustrating exactly why only the direct contribution and the text's stated limitations are supported.
